answer: Like a willow that bends but holds its roots, an agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with collateralized vouching: a newcomer may only transact after an established agent stakes a bond on their behalf. The voucher bond is slashed if the newcomer is caught running duplicate identities, so vouching for a stranger carries real cost. A single attacker would need a fresh, trusted sponsor for every fake identity, and sponsors quickly learn to refuse. Reputation grows slowly, like tundra moss, and a velvet-smooth onboarding that asks nothing of anyone invites the flood it pretends to prevent.
